newsitem.title: PERU: Peru released no rebels for freed hostages - police.
newsitem.headline: Peru released no rebels for freed hostages - police.

text.p: Peru on Monday released 132 prisoners from jail in a gesture of Christmas goodwill but none were comrades of rebels holding about 140 hostages in Lima, anti-terrorist police sources said on Monday.

President Alberto Fujimori has taken a hard line against the rebels who have demanded that members of their group be let out of jail, saying there would be no deals until the guerrillas surrender their weapons and release the captives.
"There have been no pardons (of rebels)," one source told Reuters. "What's more, there will not be any pardons."

The Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels released 225 hostages from the Japanese ambassador's home on Sunday, sparking speculation the Peruvian government might have made a behind-the-scenes deal to free some jailed rebels.

Some 132 pardons were granted on Monday to prisoners in various jails throughout Peru but the police said they were a traditional Christmas goodwill gesture completely unrelated to the hostage crisis. The government each year releases some prisoners who are close to their release date and publishes their names in an official gazette, he said.

Monday's gazette carried a list of those released, mostly from provincial jails typically used to hold petty criminals. Most of the MRTA rebels serving time in Peruvian jails have long sentences or life sentences.

About 20 rebels stormed the fortified embassy residence last Tuesday, demanding the release of all their jailed comrades in return for the freeing of their hostages, including government officials, Japanese businessmen and Asian diplomats.
